findings.title: Changing active buffer keys from Redis sets to sorted sets has no migration path
findings.body: Previously deployed workers store every `span-buf:s:*` key as a Redis Set via `SADD` and read it with `SSCAN`. This code issues `ZADD` against the same key names and later reads them with `ZSCAN`; Redis does not permit changing a key's collection type, so any unexpired legacy segment will produce `WRONGTYPE` errors when a new worker receives another span for it or tries to flush it. Since these keys can live for `redis_ttl` (one hour by default), a normal or rolling deployment can fail span batches and leave queued segments unflushable until expiry. Use versioned keys or provide a compatible migration/read path before switching types.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE corrupts end-timestamp scores for retried spans
findings.body: The new sorted-set score is `end_timestamp_precise` and is used to decide eviction, but both `ZUNIONSTORE` calls use Redis's default `SUM` aggregation. If an identical payload is already in `set_key` and is inserted again into a temporary child/parent key before redirect resolution (a normal at-least-once retry/replay scenario), the union stores that member with the sum of its timestamps rather than its actual end timestamp. Repeated retries therefore make old spans appear arbitrarily new and cause `ZPOPMIN` to evict the wrong spans. Specify an aggregation such as `AGGREGATE MAX`/`MIN` appropriate for the timestamp when merging.

findings.title: The redirect traversal limit now splits deep traces that previously merged
findings.body: The redirect walk was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 hops without another mechanism to resolve the remaining chain. For a deeply nested trace received across batches in child-before-parent order, redirects form a chain; once this loop reaches the new limit, the script maps the incoming span to an intermediate buffer rather than the root buffer. The result is multiple independently flushed segment IDs for one trace rather than one merged segment. Retain the previous bound or explicitly handle/truncate over-limit chains in a way that preserves the segment association.

findings.title: The configured max_segment_spans limit is now ignored
findings.body: `SpansBuffer` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans`, but the previous enforcement in `_load_segment_data` was removed and the Lua script always retains exactly 1,000 members. Callers configured with a lower cap can now retain up to 1,000 spans, while callers configured with a higher cap are silently limited to 1,000; even the default behavior changes from accepting 1,001 spans to retaining 1,000. Pass the configured limit to the script and use it for eviction, or remove/replace the configuration contract deliberately.

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetimes
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects this paginator while ordering by `-datetime`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime.datetime`. Calling `math.floor` on that object raises `TypeError` while building the first response cursor, causing every authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` to return HTTP 500. Even if that conversion were bypassed, `value_from_cursor` returns the numeric cursor directly, so subsequent queries would compare the database datetime column to an integer. This paginator must use DateTimePaginator's datetime serialization/deserialization behavior for this endpoint.

findings.title: Advertised negative-offset pagination raises on Django QuerySets
findings.body: The advanced branch intentionally passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative indices with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so an advanced cursor using the feature described here produces a server error instead of reverse pagination. Implement reverse traversal using valid non-negative/ranged queries, or reject negative cursors before slicing.
